A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NFIG research despite the revised title. All pages, equations, tables and figures are readable. v1 has no appendices; v2 includes readable Appendices A and B.

before.justification: v1 reports original ImageNet generation and reconstruction results, component ablations, generated images, and frequency-guidance analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including NFIG's reconstruction FID of 0.85 and generation FID of 2.81, and adds generated-image examples.

M1.justification: Both retain FR-VAE, residual vector quantization, the same frequency-band allocation, and the VAR-based autoregressive generator. DINO and AdaLN remain documented in the settings or ablations. The corrected decomposition equation expresses the already-described frequency masking rather than establishing a redesigned method.

E1.justification: Training and evaluation remain on ImageNet ILSVRC 2012, with class-conditional 256×256 generation. Video and 3D generation appear only as future directions in v2; neither appendix adds evaluated tasks or datasets.

E2.justification: v1 Table 1 and v2 Table 2 contain the same comparison methods, including VAR-d16, VAR-d20, RCG and the same GAN and diffusion baselines. FAR is newly discussed as related work but is not included in a reported comparison.

E3.justification: The reported dataset splits, metrics and experimental settings are retained, including the depth-16 generator, 350 training epochs, batch size 768, CFG 4.5 and top-k 990. No new evaluation protocol is introduced.

E4.justification: The component ablation in v1 Table 2 matches v2 Table 3. The generation-stage frequency visualizations and quantization-loss comparison against VAR also remain the same analyses, although reordered and redrawn.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or experimental uncertainty estimates. The revised loss plot does not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: The generated-image gallery expands from 24 examples in v1 Figure 5 to 28 in v2 Figure 3, retaining and rearranging the original examples. Benchmark and ablation values are unchanged. Quantization-loss labels change only through equivalent rounding.

T1.justification: Equation (1) corrects masking inside the FFT to masking the Fourier-transformed feature before inversion, fixing the mathematical expression for frequency selection. Appendix A adds explicit Fourier and spectrum definitions and an approximate spectral-decay law. The quantum-field analogy in Appendix B supplies no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain frequency-ordered autoregressive generation and FR-VAE, with the same reconstruction FID, generation FID and 1.25× speedup claim against VAR-d20. The revised abstract and frequency-resolution wording do not establish a different core contribution.

C2.justification: New Section 6 identifies inadequate first-band information capture under the scale-based frequency division and explicitly leaves video and 3D extensions unexplored. Appendix B adds a qualified conceptual analogy with quantum field theory. Interpretations of the retained experiments remain substantially unchanged.

D1.justification: v1's promise to release code upon acceptance disappears; v2 instead states that implementation builds on unspecified open-source research code. Hardware and hyperparameters remain documented. v2 also calls the unchanged 680-token sequence a vocabulary size while retaining a 4096-entry codebook, introducing a terminology inconsistency.

R1.justification: v2 adds the FAR paper, Frequency Autoregressive Image Generation with Continuous Tokens, and distinguishes it by claiming that it lacks insights into information differences across frequency bands. The remaining cited research and overall positioning are substantially retained.

P1.justification: v2 rewrites the abstract and numerous explanatory and experimental passages, reverses the related-work subsection order, reorganizes the motivation discussion, and adds a dedicated limitations section and two explanatory appendices. The title and author block also change.

P2.justification: The document changes from two columns to one. Figure 1 is redesigned, and v1's separate framework, tokenizer and decomposition diagrams are consolidated into v2 Figure 2. v2 also adds a notation table, expands and rearranges the image gallery, and restyles the frequency and loss displays.

improvement.justification: The corrected frequency-masking equation, clearer notation and consolidated diagrams improve technical readability, while Section 6 and the FAR discussion improve qualification and context. These gains are limited: experimental evidence is essentially retained, the quantum-field analogy adds no validation, and the removed code-release commitment and vocabulary terminology inconsistency weaken reproducibility information slightly.
